A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICPE research, with matching experiments and appendices A–D. The text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial additions and reorganization in v2.

before.justification: v1 Section 3 and Appendix D report original experiments measuring correctness, stopping times, regret and sampling behavior across bandits, MNIST, Magic Room, feedback graphs and binary search.

after.justification: v2 Section 4 and Appendix D retain these original experimental results alongside the expanded theoretical analysis.

M1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 specifies maximum-posterior rewards instead of the ground-truth log-probability rewards in v1's main algorithm. It also updates lambda using empirical correctness across K rollouts rather than a single soft-confidence estimate. These substantially revise the stated learning procedure, although Appendix C retains older reward formulas, leaving the implemented variant unresolved.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same deterministic and stochastic bandits, magic actions and chains, MNIST sampling, Magic Room, feedback graphs and binary search. Generalized search is emphasized in v2, but its binary-search experiment already appears in v1 Appendix D.5.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained within corresponding experiments, including DQN and I-DPT for deterministic bandits, TaS and TTPS for stochastic bandits, I-IDS for magic actions, Deep CMAB for MNIST, and TaS-FG and EXP3.G for feedback graphs. Calling I-DPT an ablation in v2 does not introduce a new comparison.

E3.justification: v2 Algorithm 1 specifies periodic critic-target copies instead of Polyak averaging and one replay minibatch instead of separate batches. Section 4 also newly states delta=0.1 for all experiments, conflicting with retained task-specific values in Appendix D. These are reported protocol revisions, without evidence of reruns; benchmark budgets, sample counts and metrics otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The policy entropy and Track-and-Stop similarity diagnostics, magic-action noise sensitivity and usage analyses, chain trajectories, MNIST class-dependent sampling and failure examples, and Magic Room clue analyses are retained. No new empirical ablation, robustness test or case study is established.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix B.1.6 adds training-accuracy certification procedures using independent rollouts, a fixed-epoch Hoeffding-bound option and an anytime sequential test with explicit confidence conditions. Their use in the reported benchmarks is not demonstrated. Existing seed counts, bootstrap confidence intervals and chi-squared testing practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical tables, empirical plots and case-study outcomes match. For example, MNIST accuracies remain 0.91, 0.66 and 0.25 for ICPE, Deep CMAB and Uniform. Magic Room, feedback-graph and binary-search results are also unchanged; v2 Table 1 redisplays binary-search results already reported in v1 Table 3.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.1 and Appendix B.1 add formal assumptions and proofs concerning policy-independent posteriors, optimal inference, fixed-budget policies, fixed-confidence duality, identifiability and training certification. The existing IDS counterexample is also revised: v1 Theorem B.1 requires K>=5, whereas v2 Theorem B.14 requires K>=7, with changed mutual-information bounds and proof.

C1.justification: v1 leaves theoretical guarantees for ICPE as future work. v2's introduction and Section 3 present theory-derived rewards and optimality/correctness results as central contributions. The narrative also emphasizes generalized search and distinct query and hypothesis spaces, while retaining the main empirical competitiveness claims.

C2.justification: v2 expands explanations of baseline applicability and reframes the oracle limitation around online simulation and training labels, adding offline training as a future direction. It removes v1's fixed-budget brittleness/curriculum conjecture and the explicit caveat that the implemented TaS stopping threshold lacks a delta-correctness proof, although that threshold remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds details about DQN's trajectory input and learned inference network, plus a reproducibility statement specifying coverage of the supplied code, configurations and experiment scripts. Hardware, principal architecture specifications, most hyperparameters and the MIT-license disclosure were already present. No new code location is provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hantoute and Lopez (2008) for the subdifferential argument and Hero and Cochran (2011) for sensor management, while pruning several background citations. It sharpens comparisons with DPT and ICEE around learned stopping and distinct action/hypothesis spaces. Most extended related work remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. v2 separates the problem setting, places theory before implementation, integrates related-work discussion into the concluding section, and presents unified training/inference pseudocode. This substantially changes the narrative and organization beyond simply inserting new scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with visibly masked image progression and a simplified exploration/inference schematic. Binary-search results are additionally displayed in the main text, while the fixed-budget stochastic plot remains only in the appendix. Headers, table formatting and placement change, but the remaining empirical graphics retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful optimality analysis, revises the IDS proof and clarifies the narrative. However, Section 3.2's maximum-posterior training losses conflict with the ground-truth log-probability losses retained in Appendix C, and the unchanged experiments do not resolve which procedure was evaluated. This leaves the connection between the new guarantees and the implemented method unclear, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
